grh_14080ed547ac440ea4d5.title: Flood Story
paragraphs: Senator Conway offers Dr. Christian an important Washington appointment heading a national medical commission, with Judy to accompany him as secretary, and the opportunity is important enough that Christian seriously considers leaving Rivers End. Before he can decide, warm rain breaks an upstream ice jam and the river floods. Christian moves through the stricken area treating injuries and directing care while Judy, Jerry Turner and Senator Conway's son Bill throw themselves into rescue work. Bill's willingness to work beside everyone else changes jealous Jerry's opinion of his romantic rival. More importantly, the emergency makes clear just how completely the town depends on its doctor. Even Bill admits that taking Christian away would cost Rivers End something it cannot replace. Christian turns down Washington and decides that he and Judy will continue doing business at the same old stand, while Jerry and Bill agree to let the best man win where Judy is concerned.

grh_1491a2470254c783a748.title: Elusive Vermeer
paragraphs: After an English country-house burglary, Harry learns that a valuable Vermeer is still missing even though police have recovered the rest of the stolen property. Hoping to sell the painting for about $150,000, he traces it through an unsuspecting family and buys the apparent old daub for £50 from a woman who has no idea what it is worth. Harry heads for his wealthy buyer with the picture under his arm, only to find Scotland Yard closing in from both directions. He instantly claims he was bringing the recovered Vermeer to the police. The story saves him from arrest, but his hoped-for fortune shrinks to the £500 insurance reward.
